the study of non-Markov dynamics of a two level atom (2LA).

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EMF when coupled to an atom, does not decohere the latter as efficiently as a reservoir does on a quantum brownian particle.
the EMF is a poor candidate for decoherence in ion trap experiments.
, the non-Markvian dynamics of a 2 LA interacting with a EMF is not as simple as one may have thought.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the non-Markoian dynamics of the 2LA in the EMF can be exactly described by the master equations we have derived.
the EMF is a good candidate for quantum information storage and processing.
, the 2LA- EMF coupling is a promising candidate to preserve maximal coherence for quantum computations, provided that the coupling is not too strong.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for quantum computation, the EMF is more efficient in decohering a 2LA than a heat bath.
, in the absence of a bath, a 2LA interacting with a resonant EMF is a quantum system which is very difficult to decohere, and this should be taken into account while designing future ion traps.
, the non-Markovianness of the EMF can be a source for preserving the coherence of the 2LA.
